corrected: No figure is wrong. Two qualifications apply. (1) "Fail-safe" here means that the EIB 3V3 loss puts the stages in their safe states (HIZ, FC clamp, /CE HIGH). With P5 LOW and regnExpected, the same loss also latches an FR-08(b) trip. A single open in R176, J101.1 or ribbon conductor 1 therefore becomes a latched availability loss; before P1, two opens were needed. (2) With P1, a 2-3 ribbon short grounds the EIB rail through conductor 2, which J201 still joins to the rail. R176 then limits the short to 15.9 mA. The design doc's 2-3 row ("held to 16 mA by R177", "rail stays >= 3.1 V") has to be rewritten. That row's "rail stays" claim already looks doubtful today, because J201 joins pins 1 and 2 on the EIB. Under P1 the short ends in the fail-safe 3V3-loss state. The EIB-rail short current falls from 31.8 mA to 15.9 mA.
evidence:
Design doc docs/charger_bq25798_wiring_design_2026-11-05.md:
- B.6 U201 row, line 1786: VCC = EIB 3V3 from ribbon pins 1 and 2, each through CR R176/R177 200 ohm. The EIB rail is 3.13 V, or 3.09 V with one conductor open.
- B.6 fault table, line 1837: "3V3 lost on the EIB (both ribbon 3V3 conductors open; one alone changes nothing)". In that state the open-drain outputs float, /CE goes HIGH (R272/R272b), Q201 turns on, Q203 off and Q202 on, so the converter goes to HIZ with the FC clamp: the safe direction. Detection: pin 7 reads LOW, which gives an FR-08(b) trip with P5 LOW and regnExpected, or a safe-direction shed with P5 HIGH.
- H.20, line 3106: CR rail 3.176 V; EIB rail 3.131 V with both conductors, 3.086 V with one. A ribbon 3V3 conductor short is 15.9 mA and 50 mW per 200 ohm 0603. An EIB rail short is 31.8 mA.
- Finding cr-eib-3v3-feed-unprotected-short, line 3790: the stated reason for two resistors is that "a single EIB resistor would lose the two-conductor redundancy". Redundancy is the only rationale given.
- B.8, lines 1931-1932 and J201 at line 1960: J101.1 is fed from R176 and J101.2 from R177. J201 pins 1 and 2 both go to EIB 3V3.

Current share: (3.176 - 3.131)/100 = 0.45 mA total in normal service, so each conductor carries about 0.23 mA. One conductor alone carries (3.176 - 3.086)/200 = 0.45 mA. This load is several orders of magnitude below any 1.27 mm contact rating. I did not fetch the Samtec FTSH/FFSD per-pin rating. No current-share or contact-rating reason for the second conductor exists.

Board: the scratchpad net dump (nets.txt) shows /J3V3_2 contains only J101.2 and R177.2, and R177.1 is on 3V3. Deleting R177 therefore removes only that net and leaves J101.2 a no-connect pad.

corrected:
These parts of the claim check out: A.8 says "pad >= 1.9 mm"; all 22 J1 pads in cr.kicad_pcb are 1.9 mm on F.Cu and B.Cu with a 1.1 mm drill; pin 10 carries up to 2.41 A; and pins 18/19 carry 1.93 A each at 60/40 sharing. Two parts need correcting.

(1) Where 1.9 mm comes from: no source exists. It first appears in commit 7bbe956 (2026-11-06, the first draft of the wiring design) without a citation. The Ag105 datasheet (Fig 11) gives only a hole diameter of 1.1 +/- 0.05 mm, with no pad size. The mating MB (Eagle .brd, package AG105) has square pads with no explicit diameter. Its DRU restring is 0.25 x drill, clamped to 10-20 mil, which gives 1.65 mm. The custom-board doc line 238 records the same 1.65 mm. So 1.9 mm is neither a datasheet value nor inherited from the MB. No current or solder-joint rationale is written anywhere: the per-pin current ratings sit in T-A-05 and T-F-16 and are tied to the pin, not the pad.

(2) "1 -> 2 tracks per gap" is wrong on pure geometry. At 1.9 mm the gap is 2.54 - 1.9 = 0.640 mm. Two 5-mil tracks with three 5-mil clearances need 5 x 0.127 = 0.635 mm. So two tracks already fit, by 5 um, which is legal under cr.kicad_dru (0.127/0.127, no outer-layer hole_clearance rule) but has zero margin. At 1.7 mm the gap is 0.840 mm: two tracks fit with 0.205 mm to spare, and three need 0.889 mm, so three do not fit. The doubling does hold for the project's grid router. gen/route_cr_pf.sh runs pathfinder.py with track and clearance both 0.127 mm on a 0.1 mm grid (0.05 mm as an option). There, the centreline band between pads is 0.640 - 2 x 0.1905 = 0.259 mm, while two centrelines need >= 0.254 mm, which rounds to 0.30 mm on either grid. That gives 1 track at 1.9 mm. At 1.7 mm the band is 0.459 mm, which gives 2 tracks. So the claim is right for the gridded router and for any routing with a practical margin, and wrong as a geometric statement. Annular ring at 1.7 mm is 0.30 mm, above the 0.15 mm DRU rule and the OSH Park 4 mil.

corrected: (a) is wrong for two of the four replacement parts. SN74LVC11A (SCLS993A) and SN74LVC2G14 (SCES200O) do specify Ioff. SN74LVC08A (SCAS283W) and SN74LVC32A (SCAS286U) do not: neither datasheet has an Ioff bullet or an Ioff row (0 occurrences of 'Ioff' in either). Their inputs are 5.5 V tolerant with negative-only clamp diodes, so a powered input should not physically back-feed VCC. However, nothing in the datasheet guarantees that leakage at VCC = 0. Both Teensy-driven inputs that B.7 depends on, CHG_ARM/P5 (U114 gate A) and FCCEIL (U116 gate A), would move onto the SN74LVC08A. To keep a datasheet-guaranteed Ioff, the consolidation needs Ioff-rated AND parts (keep the 2G08s for U114/U116, or choose a quad AND whose datasheet specifies Ioff), or B.7 has to be re-worded to rely on 'over-voltage-tolerant inputs, no positive input clamp' and checked on the bench (T-C-07 back-feed ammeter). Minor point on the 11A: its Ioff row is +/-10 uA at VCC = 0 V, but the printed test condition is 'VI or VO = VCC', which means 0 V. That is a much weaker guarantee than the LVC1G/2G condition of 'VI or VO = 5.5 V' (SCES200O). The package count is correct: 13 packages become 7 (11A, 2 x 08A, 32A, 2G14, plus U111/U113 unchanged). (b) is confirmed.
evidence: B.7 row 'CR 3V3 lost while armed (T6 open; r2)' (docs/charger_bq25798_wiring_design_2026-11-05.md:1862) says '(Teensy may still drive; LVC Ioff blocks back-feed through the inputs)'. B.3 header (line 1650) lists Ioff as a property of every logic part. CHG_ARM goes straight to U105 pin 3 and U114 pin 1 with only R108 (47 kOhm pull-down), lines 472, 1918 and 1926. FCCEIL goes straight to U116 gate A with only R124 (47 kOhm pull-down), lines 670, 1489 and 1666. Neither input has a series resistor. TI SN74LVC08A SCAS283W (Jul 2024): the Features list has no Ioff bullet and the Electrical Characteristics have no Ioff row. Section 7.3.3 states 'The inputs to this device have negative clamping diodes. The outputs ... have both positive and negative clamping diodes'. Section 7.3.4 covers over-voltage tolerant inputs. Abs max VI is -0.5 to 6.5 V and VO is -0.5 to VCC+0.5 V. TI SN74LVC32A SCAS286U (Jul 2024): no Ioff anywhere, inputs accept 5.5 V, same absolute-maximum structure. TI SN74LVC11A SCLS993A (May 2024): Ioff +/-10 uA at VCC 0 V, condition 'VI or VO = VCC'. TI SN74LVC2G14 SCES200O (Aug 2015): Features include 'Ioff Supports Live Insertion, Partial-Power-Down Mode, and Back-Drive Protection', and Ioff is +/-10 uA at VCC 0 with VI or VO = 5.5 V. Renesas SLG46826 datasheet Rev 3.25 (3-Aug-2026): Table 3 lists 'DC Input Voltage GND - 0.5 V to VDD + 0.5 V'. The note on p.117 reads 'There are ESD Diodes between pin VDD and pin GND on each pin. Exceeding VDD results in leakage current on the input pin, and VDD will be pulled up, following the voltage on the input pin.' So a Teensy pin driving CHG_ARM or FCCEIL HIGH at 3.3 V, with no series resistor, would lift the unpowered CR rail to about 2.7 V. That is above the LVC 1.65 V and TLV3012 1.8 V minimums that B.7 uses to argue the 0.3-0.45 V BAV199 residual is harmless.
